I’ll read the repository instructions and the specified qualification scope, then assemble the two host composition checks within the owned directory. All execution will stay offline; I’ll leave hardware, builds, and frozen inputs untouched.

The scope confirms the missing boundary: E97 tested stdio over host files, while the VFS tests omitted stdio. I’ll combine the corrected E97 sources with the unchanged LittleFS coalescing path and keep WEL as a documented pairing link only.

The copied `fclose` path includes real VFS close handling, including inode release when close reports an error. I’ll retain those function bodies and shim the host descriptor table, scheduler bookkeeping, and allocation interfaces. The fault checks will run at the NOR callbacks, after native code has copied read bytes or begun COW writes.

The fixture now covers the forced read-window miss and two delivery modes for the dirty-node failure: deferred `fsync`, and `O_SYNC` during `fflush`. I’ll check public returns and stream state, full-file content after reopen/remount, and resource release. Each attempt will retain its manifest and raw output.

Both boundaries passed under ASan/UBSan. Native LittleFS copied 4092 bytes into the refill buffer before the NOR read returned EIO; stdio invalidated the mapping, and both retries reached the sticky VFS error. The sync failures propagated through `fflush`/`fsync`/`fclose`, released all tracked resources, and reopened/remounted as one complete new file.

`O_SYNC` also showed why position must be checked separately: the failed delivery left VFS at 4110 while `ftello` reported 4130 with 20 bytes still buffered. I’ll record that error-path state and its recovery limit explicitly.

The evidence package is complete: two boundary checks, three fault executions, and six full-file size/EOF checks passed.
